verdict: Caution: lend selectively to re-rollers with own conversion margin and tight working-capital control; avoid pure merchant billet-to-TMT converters with thin spreads and leveraged balance sheets.
title: Tarapur steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Tarapur re-roller buys billets or scrap, heats and rolls them into TMT bars, and sells to builders, dealers and infrastructure contractors. **Cash is made on the conversion spread, not on the steel price** — the mill earns a fixed rolling margin per tonne while the billet price passes through. So when a proposal lands, check the conversion margin per tonne and the billet-to-TMT spread; if the spread is thin, ask how the unit protects margin (back-to-back orders, brand premium, value-added grades). Tarapur MIDC is primarily a chemicals and pharma cluster, with steel concentrated at Wada nearby [1]; local steel-specific data is thin, so lean on first principles and peer results.

## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in brand and dealer network, not in the furnace. Captain Steel built a premium over market through brand ambassadors and national advertising [9], and that premium is the buffer when spreads compress. **Working capital is the real risk: inventory of billets plus 30-60 day dealer receivables tie up cash**, and rating reports flag moderately high working-capital needs supported by bank lines [11] and leveraged structures where gearing rose to 1.80x from 1.40x on debt-funded expansion [10].

## What has changed now
The data pack reads Caution at 47 [D]. Maharashtra GST collections are running 8.6% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D] — a genuine local demand tailwind — but electricity demand is up only 6.0% versus India's 9.5% [D], a local stress signal that industrial activity in the state is lagging. India-wide IIP for NIC 24 (basic metals) is +2.4% YoY and +3.4% Apr-to-date [D]. **Peer results are strong but not local**: Steel Exchange India posted ~₹340 crore Q2 FY27 revenue, up ~45% YoY [6]; Rathi Steel revenue over ₹200 crore, up over 30% YoY with volume up ~28.86% [7]; JSW Steel Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 20% with gearing down to 0.42 [5]. These are large, integrated players — do not read them as Tarapur re-roller health.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue re-rollers with a branded TMT line, own dealer network, and part-integration (captive rolling plus power)** — the MITC-type partly integrated model that rating agencies reward for operational synergies [8]. Structure term loans with a moratorium matched to ramp-up, and take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, drawing-power reconciliation, and a quarterly conversion-margin certificate. **Take every month: stock statement, debtor ageing, and power-consumption units per tonne rolled** — units per tonne is the cleanest proxy for whether the mill is actually running.

## Early-warning signs
- **Electricity units per tonne falling while sales rise** — possible trading rather than rolling; ask for the rolling-mill log. - **Dealer receivables stretching beyond 60 days** — check whether sales are being pushed on credit; tighten drawing power. - **Billet purchase price rising faster than TMT realisations** — margin squeeze; ask for the latest order book and spread.
watch: Inventory days rise above 60 or receivables beyond 60 days -> freeze drawing power enhancement and seek debtor ageing
Units per tonne fall >10% while sales rise -> inspect rolling-mill log; possible trading not rolling
Spread per tonne compresses below the sanctioned threshold -> reprice or reduce limit
GST turnover trails bank-statement sales by >10% -> investigate unrecorded sales or circular billing
